parsed.corrected_rationale: The comment begins with "4." which is likely a comment number rather than a reference to a specific section, table, or figure in the paper. However, the comment does reference a specific and unique aspect of the paper: it identifies that the paper essentially proposes a loss (the vMF-based loss) to train the network to improve OOD detection, i.e., its core methodological contribution. This is clearly the paper's central method, so the addressed part is obvious to the authors, even though no section number is named; the missing comparisons would obviously relate to the related work and experimental comparison sections. Furthermore, the comment clearly specifies what needs to be addressed: citation of and comparison with specific prior approaches (IsoMax, Scaled Cosine, DUQ, IsoMax+, SNGP) and clarification of whether using vMF helps at all. Since the comment addresses a part of the paper that is obvious to the authors and specifies concretely what needs to be addressed, it is both well grounded and highly specific.
